name: Reproducibility Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for reproducibility, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for reproducibility, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When reproducibility guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. Surface known limitations of a chosen reproducibility approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
3. Prefer the simplest reproducibility approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to reproducibility (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. Prefer explicit, readable reproducibility solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
6. Keep reproducibility outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. Keep reproducibility changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
8. State assumptions about reproducibility explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
9. Before starting reproducibility work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
10. Validate reproducibility outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
11. When multiple reproducibility strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting reproducibility assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new reproducibility abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated reproducibility concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of reproducibility correctness.
- Do not silently drop reproducibility edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these reproducibility guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
